[[File:Avocado soup.jpg|thumb|Avocado soup garnished with [[caviar]]]]

'''Avocado soup''' is a [[fruit soup]] prepared using [[avocado]]s as a primary ingredient.<ref name="Sackett Pestka Gisslen 2010"/><ref name="Rombauer Becker Becker Guarnaschelli 1997"/><ref name="Sandler 1970"/> Other ingredients can include milk, cream, or [[buttermilk]]; soup [[stock (cooking)|stock]] or [[broth]]; lime juice, lemon juice, and salt and pepper.<ref name="Sackett Pestka Gisslen 2010"/><ref name="Rombauer Becker Becker Guarnaschelli 1997"/><ref name="Sandler 1970"/><ref name="Ried 2015"/><ref name="Devi 1988"/> Additional ingredients used can include onions, [[shallots]], garlic, [[hot sauce]], [[cilantro]], [[red pepper]], [[cayenne pepper]] and [[cumin]]; water can be used to thin the soup.<ref name="Rombauer Becker Becker Guarnaschelli 1997"/><ref name="Sandler 1970"/><ref name="Gourmet Traveller 2017"/><ref name="Ried 2015"/><ref name="ABC News 2015"/> It is eaten widely in areas of Mexico.

The avocados in the soup itself are typically [[purée]]d or mashed; sliced, diced or cubed avocado can be used as a garnish.<ref name="Sackett Pestka Gisslen 2010"/><ref name="Rombauer Becker Becker Guarnaschelli 1997"/><ref name="Sandler 1970"/><ref name="Sellick 2010"/><ref name="Tradition Publishers 2009"/> Additional garnishes can include sliced lime, sour cream, chives, crab meat, shrimp and [[salsa fresca]].<ref name="Rombauer Becker Becker Guarnaschelli 1997"/><ref name="Sandler 1970"/><ref name="Ried 2015"/><ref name="Bittman 2014"/> It can be prepared and served as a cold or hot soup.<ref name="Sackett Pestka Gisslen 2010"/><ref name="Rombauer Becker Becker Guarnaschelli 1997"/><ref name="Sandler 1970"/>

Avocado soup's color can change as time passes because oxidation causes avocados to brown, but this does not affect the soup's flavor.<ref name="Ried 2015"/>
